items.title: Every object of the derived category of an inverse system of rings is represented by a system of K-flat complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for an inverse system of rings (A_n), every object K of the derived category of the module-valued inverse systems can be represented by a system of complexes (K_n^bullet) with each K_n^bullet K-flat (source lines 23815-23821). The proof is an induction that resolves the compatibility problem between the two structures. It first uses the preceding lemma to represent K by a system of complexes (M_n^bullet) all of whose transition maps M_{n+1}^bullet -> M_n^bullet are surjective (proof lines 23824-23826). It then chooses a quasi-isomorphism K_1^bullet -> M_1^bullet with K_1^bullet K-flat, possible by the K-flat resolution lemma (proof lines 23827-23829). The inductive step is the substantive part: assuming K_n^bullet -> ... -> K_1^bullet and maps psi_e : K_e^bullet -> M_e^bullet have been constructed so that the displayed squares commute for all e < n, the proof forms a diagram in D(A_{n+1}) and, because M_{n+1}^bullet -> M_n^bullet is termwise surjective, constructs the complex C^bullet fitting in the upper left corner with terms the fibred products C^p = M_{n+1}^p times_{M_n^p} K_n^p, which is quasi-isomorphic to M_{n+1}^bullet in a step the author states is omitted (proof lines 23830-23852). Choosing a quasi-isomorphism K_{n+1}^bullet -> C^bullet with K_{n+1}^bullet K-flat then completes the induction (proof lines 23853-23855). The non-routine content is the termwise surjectivity reduction and the fibred-product construction that makes the induction step possible.
